## What this dashboard shows

- Tracks whether 5 acquisitions are delivering on their investment thesis by monitoring 3 levers per deal (cash, growth, margin) against targets, using live KPI actuals from the CFO Cockpit for FY2026 Jan-Jul.
- Overall status: No deal has every lever on track; 3 levers are off track and 5 levers are at risk.
- ₹210.72B of FY2026 EBITDA to date (₹206.01B at Wipro's stake) sits in the 3 deals with an off-track lever.

## What to report

- Cash performance is the primary concern: Wipro Consumer Care International at 207 days DSO against 90 days target (off track), Wipro Infrastructure Engineering at 103 days against 90 days (off track), and Wipro Kawasaki Precision Machinery at 63 days against 60 days (at risk).
- Growth levers are underperforming across three deals: Wipro Kawasaki Precision Machinery 8.4% vs 12.0% target (off track), Wipro Infrastructure Engineering 9.9% vs 12.0% (at risk), and Wipro Consumer Care India 8.0% vs 10.0% (at risk).
- Margin performance is stable with only minor misses: Wipro GE Healthcare at 17.9% vs 18.0% target and Wipro Kawasaki Precision Machinery at 14.8% vs 15.0%, both at risk but within tolerance.
- The off-track levers trace to specific ERP accounts: 18 SAP S/4HANA accounts for Consumer Care International, 12 SAP S/4HANA accounts for Infrastructure Engineering, and 2 Tally Prime accounts for Kawasaki.

## Watch out for

- Deal values, theses and lever targets are illustrative (simulated); only actuals are live—company 1 uses real SAP BDC data while companies 2–5 are simulated ERP data. Question: When will all companies be on live ERP feeds?
- The dashboard shows "illustrative (demo)" as a source qualifier and notes the data is "built in Snowflake (group context)," indicating this may be a prototype rather than production reporting.
- Consumer Care International shows extreme DSO variance (207 vs 90 days, +117 days over target) yet reports strong growth (34.3% vs 20.0%) and margin (61.1% vs 55.0%) performance. Question: Is the cash issue a timing/acquisition integration artifact or a structural working capital problem?
- Wipro Kawasaki Precision Machinery is the only deal with all three levers either off track or at risk (cash at risk, growth off track, margin at risk), despite contributing only ₹9.61B EBITDA at 51% stake. Question: Should this deal be escalated for remediation or exit review?
